Operator Runbook - Bench Evaporation Plant, Rev A
Synthetic hackathon engineering evidence
1. Pre-start
Confirm B1 contains the water-rich initial charge and B2 contains the concentrated NaCl initial charge.
Confirm manual drain valves V26 and V27 are closed and cooling-water valves V13, V17 and V29 are aligned for service.
Confirm condenser cooling-water flow indication FIS-801 is available before heating.
Verify B6 and B7 are sufficiently empty for the next batch.
2. Automatic batch observation
Normal operator observation is B3 fill/mix -> B4 buffer -> B5 charge -> heating/evaporation -> simultaneous condensate/concentrate finishing branches -> return pumping. The controller owns the automated valve set; do not manually override an automated valve during an acceptance run.
3. Expected qualitative trends
Variable | Expected trend
B3 level | Rises during water and brine charge, then falls while V11 transfers to B4.
B3 concentration | Changes primarily while V9 adds brine; then remains approximately constant until discharge.
B5 temperature | Rises during heating, then plateaus near composition-dependent boiling temperature.
B5 concentration | Rises during evaporation until target is reached.
B6 level | Rises as condensate is produced; later falls during return pumping.
B7 level | Rises when V15 transfers concentrate; later falls during return pumping.
4. Abnormal indications
Repeated tiny integration steps near a tank port level may indicate missing hysteresis or non-regularized port loss equations.
Oscillation at the B5 boiling transition may indicate missing Q_up anti-chattering logic.
A WaterNaCl simulation that stalls at pump start is a known legacy numerical issue; first validate the same topology with StandardWater.
Do not resolve return-routing questions from pump location alone; check the approved routing change record.
